title: Are route reviews every 3 s paying for anything?
question: The runtime re-asks the provider every 3 s while it travels. In run B, 79 such reviews changed nothing. Would reviewing every 6 s save calls without changing outcomes?
hypothesis: Stretching the travel review from 3 s to 6 s cuts provider requests by at least 20 per journey and changes neither completion, total time (within 5 s) nor the coffee (within 2 points).

motivation.observation: Run B: 79 of Jev's 212 decisions (37%) were mid-route reviews and 0 of 79 changed the plan. The scripted baseline spends 76 of its 155 calls the same way. NEXT_MODEL.md makes 6 s a tripwire at < 1% plan changes over ≥ 5 live runs; this experiment measures the other half of that trade, what reviews cost and what dropping half of them changes in the world.
evidence: bun run trace docs/traces/jev-after-hours-live-2026-09-27.json: 79 reviews kept the plan, 0 replaced a running action

successCriteria: at least 20 fewer requests per journey with no change in completion, time or coffee
falsificationCriteria: fewer than 20 requests saved (reviews are not where the calls go)
completion, time (> 5 s) or coffee (> 2 points) changes: reviews are doing work
limitations: The scripted baseline rarely changes its mind, so this measures the cost of reviews and the effect of fewer reviews on the world, not how often a model would use a review to correct itself. The tripwire in NEXT_MODEL.md still needs ≥ 5 live runs for that.
Does not change the product default: this is evidence for the tripwire, not the tripwire.
